title: The holy horse
translation: The priest of Toganoo was walking along the road one day. Down by the river a man was washing a horse, and he kept saying to it, "Ashi, ashi!" Foot, foot: lift your foot. But to a priest, ashi sounds like a-ji, "the letter A", the sacred syllable that esoteric Buddhists meditate on.
The priest stopped. "How holy! This man must have merit from his past lives coming to fruit. He's chanting 'A, A'! Whose horse is this? It moves me so much."
"It's the horse of the fushō, sir," the man said, meaning a clerk in the palace guards. The priest heard fushō, "unborn".
"How wonderful! 'The letter A is unborn from the beginning.' Of course! What a blessed bond I've made today." And he wiped away tears of joy.
original: {栂尾|とがのを}の{上人|しやうにん}{道|みち}を{過|す}ぎたまひけるに、{河|かは}にて{馬|うま}{洗|あら}ふ{男|をとこ}、「あしあし。」といひければ、
{上人|しやうにん}たちとまりて、「あなたふとや。{宿執|しゆくしふ}{開発|かいほつ}の{人|ひと}かな。{阿字々々|あじあじ}と{唱|とな}ふるぞや。いかなる{人|ひと}の{御馬|おんま}ぞ。あまりにたふとく{覚|おぼ}ゆるは。」と{尋|たづ}ね{給|たま}ひければ、
「{府生殿|ふしやうどの}の{御馬|おんま}に{候|さうらふ}。」と{答|こた}へけり。
「こはめでたきことかな。{阿字本不生|あじほんふしやう}にこそあなれ。うれしき{結縁|けちえん}をもしつるかな。」とて、{感涙|かんるい}を{拭|のご}はれけるとぞ。
literal: When the holy man of Toganoo was passing along the road, a man washing a horse in the river said 'Ashi, ashi', and so
the holy man stopped and asked: 'Ah, how holy! He is a person in whom the karma of former lives has opened. He is chanting "A-ji, A-ji". Whose horse is this? I feel it is so very holy.'
'It is the horse of Lord Fushō', he answered.
'Oh, how splendid! It is "the letter A is originally unborn". What a joyful bond I have made', he said, and they say he wiped away tears of emotion.

notes.text: Myōe (1173–1232), who lived at Kōzanji in Toganoo, in the mountains north-west of Kyoto. He was a monk of the Kegon school (the 1925 edition calls him the restorer of the school), and he also practised esoteric Buddhism. He was famous for his strict and very pure devotion.

The 1925 edition: the man said 'foot' ({足|あし}) because he was washing the horse's legs, and Myōe heard {阿字|あじ}. In the spelling of the time, あし and あじ were often written the same, with no mark for the voiced sound.

{宿執|しゆくしふ}: the karma you carry from past lives; {開発|かいほつ}: 'opening, coming to fruit'. The 1925 edition: a person in whom the merit gained in a former life appears in this one. Myōe is sure the man is a hidden saint.
{阿字|あじ}: the letter A, the first sound of the Sanskrit alphabet. In esoteric Buddhism it stands for the origin of all things, and meditating on it is a central practice.
{府生|ふしやう}: a low-ranking clerk in one of the guard offices of the palace (the 1925 edition). It sounds exactly like {不生|ふしやう}, 'unborn'.

notes.quote: 阿字本不生にこそあなれ
notes.text: {阿字本不生|あじほんふしやう}: 'the letter A is originally unborn', the esoteric teaching that the source of everything was never born and never dies. To Myōe, a man who says 'A' about the horse of 'unborn' is reciting the whole doctrine. あなれ is あるなれ with る dropped: 'it surely is'.

notes.quote: うれしき結縁をもしつるかな
notes.text: {結縁|けちえん}: making a bond with the Buddha's teaching, which helps you towards salvation later. Myōe treats the meeting as a gift.

notes.quote: 感涙を拭はれけるとぞ
notes.text: {感涙|かんるい}: tears of emotion, the same word as at the end of section 236. There Shōkai's tears were wasted. Here the text simply stops on Myōe's tears and says nothing more.
